history.period: 10th century CE (temple construction); the nine-lakh-rupee legend dates to V.S. 969 (912-913 CE) in one account
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE -- keep-or-drop decision needed: the Navlakha (Naulakha) Jain Temple in Pali city is a 10th-century Shvetambara Jain temple dedicated to Parshvanath (mulnayak is a white idol of Navlakha Parshvanath in padmasana), documented in the ASI/IGNCA archaeological inventory (RJ/PLI-047). Its name comes from a legend that Rs 9 lakh were spent on its construction in V.S. 969 -- supposedly the cost of the ghee saved, the money then being used for the temple. It stands behind the collectorate in the heart of Pali city and is noted for its elaborate carvings, curvilinear shikharas, serpentine cusped arches at the entrance, and a colonnaded hall with lotus-panel ceilings. Dharamshala and bhojanshala facilities are available. The CSV name 'Naulakha Jain Temple | Pali' is correct for Pali city -- note that there is a separate, well-known Naulakha temple at Hansi in Haryana, which is a different shrine (do not conflate the two).

name: Naulakha Jain Temple
town_description: Pali, in the Marwar region between Jodhpur and Udaipur, is an ancient trading city once ruled by the Guhilas, Chauhans and later the Rathores of Marwar; it is a major industrial and textile centre of western Rajasthan.
